_readme: Single source of truth for the coordinator doc-type registry AND the cross-repo identity registries. Read at load time by BOTH the Python CLIs (coordinator-doc-new, cross-repo-memo, coordinator-lesson-promote, coordinator-queue-append via bin/lib/coordinator_registry.py) AND the Python write-guard modules (formerly hooks/scripts/validate-frontmatter-schema.py; the live logic is claude-klabauter coordinator_core/write_guards/validate_frontmatter_schema_{deny,advisory}.py, evaluated in-process by coordinator/hooks/scripts/preuse-write-dispatch.py) [Review: code-reviewer — deleted file no longer a live consumer; live logic now the claude-klabauter write_guards port]. Replaces three former hand-maintained JS mirrors + the 3x _REPO_KEY_ALIASES Python triplication. NEVER rename to *.schema.json or *.yaml — the schema loader globs both and would parse this as a JSON-Schema record. The *.manifest.json suffix is a load-bearing glob-avoidance constraint. Spec: docs/plans/2026-07-02-shared-coordinator-registry-manifest.md.

spinoff.authoringHint: Spinoffs are PM-gated forks — the canonical authoring path is the /spinoff skill (or coordinator:roadmap-planning).

spinoff-roadmap.authoringHint: Roadmap stubs are authored by the coordinator:roadmap-planning skill, which supplies --roadmap-id / --stub-id.

recovery.authoringHint: Recovery handoffs reconstruct state after a crashed session — the canonical authoring path is `coordinator-doc-new --type recovery` directly (no dedicated skill).

_reconstruction: KNOWN_TYPES = {d.type for d in docTypes} ∪ set(queueTypes). docTypes is complete over every non-queue type (offerable and excluded alike), so this union byte-equals the pre-refactor coordinator-doc-new._KNOWN_TYPES. It is also a superset-safe match for the plan's pinned formula {docTypes} ∪ {kindOfferOverride.values()} ∪ queueTypes ∪ {lesson}, since spinoff/roadmap-baton/lesson already appear as docTypes entries. SIDECAR_TYPES = {d.type for d in docTypes if d.isSidecar}. QUEUE_TYPES = queueTypes. The C2 golden-tuple test MUST assert byte-equality against the current tuples.

identity._retiredCentralReceiverIdsNote: Retired central-EM ids mapped to their live successor. These are NOT receiver aliases and MUST keep failing at send -- their absence from centralReceiverIds is the operative rule. This map is read only AFTER a send has already failed, so the did-you-mean names the real successor instead of a fuzzy match. Without it, difflib over registered receivers points the operator at an unrelated repo. Declarative here rather than pinned in a consumer, for the reason _redirectAliasesNote records: two copies of this identity data drift.
identity._aliasDirections: repoAliases stores the canonical triple per divergent identity. Python REPO_ALIASES = {registryKey: shortname}. JS REPO_BASENAME_TO_EM_SHORTNAME = {dirBasename: shortname}. cross-repo-memo RECEIVER_EM_ALIASES = {shortname: registryKey} (inverse). dirBasename = registryKey with underscores→dashes, stored explicitly rather than derived so the convention is never silently assumed. Every OTHER fleet repo registers under its conventional key (shortname with dashes→underscores, per claude-klabauter's convention_repo_key); the one row present is a genuine divergence — the example-game-repo repo's working-tree basename is `example-game-workbench-repo`, not the conventional `example-game-repo`, so em_id_for_basename() cannot derive its shortname from the basename alone. NEGATIVE-SPEC: registryKey is the MACHINE-LOCAL registry key (`repos.example_game_workbench_repo`), never the shortname — claude-klabauter's coordinator_registry.py builds REPO_ALIASES = {registryKey: shortname} and RECEIVER_EM_ALIASES as its inverse, so a registryKey equal to the shortname degrades the row to a no-op identity mapping and breaks _receiver_repo_key, em_id_for_root, and the parent-folder-scan fallback (7 live claude-klabauter test failures, 2026-08-05). The key itself must stay present — coordinator_registry.py indexes identity.repoAliases under a required-key KeyError guard, so deleting it is an install-integrity failure. Adding a row is a last resort for a repo that genuinely cannot register conventionally; note that a row makes receiver_em_to_repo_key resolve THROUGH the alias, so the aliased repo's conventional key becomes unreachable while the row exists.
identity._redirectAliasesNote: redirectAliases lists DoE-canonical home/mirror receiver ids that always redirect to the first entry of centralReceiverIds (doe-claude-em) — they are NOT distinct working trees, just this same central surface under another name (~/.claude / coordinator-claude are the live-install of THIS repo). Promoted from cross-repo-memo's former code-pinned _DOE_CANONICAL_REDIRECT_ALIASES literal (2026-07-21) so DoE and its downstream consumer share one declarative source instead of two copies that can drift. Cross-repo contract surface: claude-klabauter's coordinator_core/ops/fleet/_memo_resolver.py `read_redirect_aliases()` reads this field declaratively (their negative-spec forbids hardcoding it on their side) and degrades to an empty set if this field is ever removed — do not delete without checking that consumer.
